text:  Foundations > Logistic Regression Engineering AI Agents Logistic regression is used in machine learning extensively - every time we need to provide probabilistic semantics to an outcome e.g. predicting the risk of developing a given disease (e.g. diabetes; coronary heart disease), based on observed characteristics of the patient (age, sex, body mass index, results of various blood tests, etc.), whether an voter will vote for a given party, predicting the probability of failure of a given process, system or product, predicting a customer’s propensity to purchase a product or halt a subscription, predicting the likelihood of a homeowner defaulting on a mortgage. Odds and the Logistic Sigmoid If is a probability of an event, then the ratio is the corresponding odds, the ratio of the event occurring divided by not occurring. For example, if a race horse runs 100 races and wins 25 times and loses the other 75 times, the probability of winning is 25/100 = 0.25 or 25%, but the odds of the horse winning are 25/75 = 0.333 or 1 win to 3 loses.
